newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares close lower after notably quiet day.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares close lower after notably quiet day.

text.p: 1620 GMT - Swedish shares ended Wednesday on a softer note in line with other European bourses, pressured by profit-taking. Trade was notably thin throughout the day.
"The market just ran out of steam. It was an extremely quiet day," a broker said.

Engineering industry suffered the largest setbacks with telecoms group Ericsson in the forefront. * Stockholm general index falls 0.79 percent to 2763.46 * Turnover moderate 3.97 billion crowns * Ericsson dipped five crowns to 265.5. Drugs major Astra closed 1.5 crowns lower at 372.
Swedish shares drifted lower in notably quiet trade to end Wednesday on a softer note in line with other bourses in Europe.
The Stockholm bourse general index dipped 0.79 percent to 2763.46 in turnover of 3.79 billion crowns. Profit-taking hampered trade and all sectors were hit.

Engineering industry suffered the largest setbacks, with telecoms group Ericsson bearing the brunt, falling five crowns to 265.5. Ericsson generated almost 25 percent of the volume on the Stockholm bourse during the Wednesday.
"There was nothing specific pressuring Ericsson, the whole sector was weak today," an analyst said.
Household appliance group Electrolux AB followed suit and ended 10.5 crowns lower at 492.5.
Drugs major Astra slipped 1.5 crowns to 372 while its collegue Pharmacia & Upjohn was down 0.5 crowns at 301.
There is no consensus as to what direction the bourse will take on Thursday.
"Sellers are not aggresive, so it's possible it will come back up tomorrow," one broker said.
